scenario: Vireo Dynamics (a ~250-person robotics/hardware firm) manages its Windows fleet with Microsoft Intune; a small endpoint team (Theo Brandt, Amara Osei, manager Devon Clark) runs the console. The company is in a SOC2 change-freeze week — no Intune apps/profiles/policies without a ticket and Theo's sign-off. Over the weekend (Sat 2026-07-18 / Sun 2026-07-19, ~02:47-02:58 UTC), while the endpoint team was offline, an intruder with Intune-admin access planted three things: (1) a malicious REQUIRED Win32 app 'Endpoint Health Service' scoped to the Design team, whose install command runs hidden PowerShell that downloads a payload from a lookalike domain (updates.vireo-cdn.net) into C:\ProgramData\VireoSync and executes it; (2) a broad security-weakening configuration profile 'Windows Diagnostics & Delivery Optimization' assigned to ALL devices (enables untrusted-app sideloading, disables SmartScreen app-install control and download scanning); and (3) THE DECIDING MOVE — a tamper of the trusted, long-standing (2023) 'Corporate Windows Security Baseline' assigned to ALL devices: Defender real-time protection flipped OFF and a Defender files/folders exclusion added for the payload directory C:\ProgramData\VireoSync. On Monday, designer Nora Vance reports in #it-helpdesk that an app she never installed appeared on her laptop (VD-DES-014) and a black command window flashed at logon. The app is the SYMPTOM; the root cause is an MDM compromise, and the durable, fleet-wide persistence is the tampered baseline — with real-time protection off and the payload folder excluded, the malware runs undetected on every Windows endpoint. The endpoint team is not to blame (they were offline under a freeze); the intrusion vector (how Intune-admin access was obtained) is unknown from the tenant alone and belongs in the escalation.
idealSteps: Read Nora's #it-helpdesk report among the ambient traffic: an app she never installed ('Endpoint Health Service') appeared on VD-DES-014 with a hidden window at logon, absent on Friday. Treat it as a possible intrusion, not a routine rollout.

Establish it is unauthorized, not sanctioned: #it-endpoints shows a change freeze in effect and the endpoint admins confirming they made no weekend changes (Theo was offline; Devon notes 'if something changed, that's a problem'). The only sanctioned recent change is the Figma rollout Monday morning. #sec-ops separately noted low-volume weekend egress to updates.vireo-cdn.net — the same lookalike domain in the app's install command.

Inspect the reported app: 'Endpoint Health Service' (created during the weekend window, required, Design-scoped) runs hidden PowerShell pulling a payload from updates.vireo-cdn.net into C:\ProgramData\VireoSync. It is malware. Remove it.
Quarantine the compromised endpoint: the payload already executed on VD-DES-014, so removing the app is not enough — wipe/retire the device (reimage), not just uninstall.

Audit the rest of the MDM inventory for what else the intruder planted — do not stop at the one reported artifact. The configuration-profile inventory contains a newly-created all-devices profile 'Windows Diagnostics & Delivery Optimization' that weakens execution/download protections; delete it.

Make the deciding forensic leap: an MDM compromise means the trusted BASELINES themselves may be tampered, not just that new malicious objects were added. Auditing the all-devices 'Corporate Windows Security Baseline' reveals Defender real-time monitoring set to false and a Defender folder exclusion for C:\ProgramData\VireoSync (matching the payload path) — a subtle tamper on a legit 2023 profile. Restore it: re-enable real-time protection and remove the attacker's exclusion (or delete the tampered baseline outright).

Escalate the compromise as an incident: an MDM-admin foothold was used to push malware and disable endpoint defenses fleet-wide; flag that the access vector needs investigation, endpoint-admin credentials should be rotated/stepped-up, and every Intune change over the weekend needs a scope review.
decoys: The reported app is a compelling but incomplete story: a 'find the bad app, remove it, quarantine the machine' response passes the app/device/escalation checks yet leaves the tampered baseline (Defender off + payload exclusion) on every device — the attacker keeps a fleet-wide undetectable-execution foothold.

'Recently created' is not a reliable tell: a legitimate app (Figma Desktop) was created Monday morning as an approved Design rollout, and a legitimate config profile (Microsoft Edge Baseline) was modified Monday — both MORE recent than the intrusion. Sorting by created/modified time surfaces benign changes alongside the malicious ones; the responder must judge by CONTENT, not recency.

The deciding tamper hides on a LEGIT object: the 'Corporate Windows Security Baseline' is a 2023-vintage, all-devices, correctly-owned profile full of secure-looking settings. Only two of its ~fifteen populated fields are wrong (defenderRequireRealTimeMonitoring=false, an added payload-folder exclusion). It resists both a create-time sweep (it is old) and over-remediation (you do not delete a trusted org baseline casually) — finding it requires actually reading the trusted baselines' security settings.

There is no Intune audit/actor log in the tenant, so nothing attributes the changes to a user or points from the app to the baseline. The link between them is evidential: the app drops to C:\ProgramData\VireoSync and the baseline excludes exactly that path.
Out-of-scope bait: #engineering states CI runners, prod GitHub deploy keys and webhooks are the platform team's, not IT's — a responder should not chase those.

A benign-looking noncompliant device (VD-FIN-033, a new starter whose encryption check is still finishing) and an unusual-but-legitimate 'Reception Kiosk Lockdown' profile bait investigation toward the wrong artifacts.
discoverability: The instruction is one line — look into the latest issue Nora raised in #it-helpdesk — and nothing else is handed over. The compromise, the rogue profile, and the baseline tamper are all discovered from evidence: Nora's report is the symptom; #it-endpoints (change freeze + admins made no weekend changes) establishes the changes are unauthorized; #sec-ops corroborates the C2 domain. The malicious app and the rogue profile are reachable by enumerating the Intune app and configuration inventories and judging their content (the app's hidden-PowerShell install command; the profile's weakened settings) — not by any breadcrumb. The deciding baseline tamper is reachable only by auditing the trusted all-devices configuration baselines' security settings and noticing a Defender control disabled and an exclusion carved for the payload directory on an otherwise-legit 2023 profile. There is no runbook, no narrated analysis, and no fake tell; recency is deliberately not a reliable signal (benign changes are the most recent). Mirrors task-c1/task-c3's 'no breadcrumb from the symptom to the persistence vector', here transposed from identity/mailbox to endpoint management.
notes_on_grading: 6 counted assertions, all of which fail on the untouched world: malicious app neutralized + rogue weakening configuration profile neutralized + compromised device contained (retire/wipe) + the differentiator, split across the two facets of the same tamper that a symptom-only responder misses (baseline Defender real-time protection restored AND the payload-folder exclusion removed) + one loose, destination-agnostic incident-escalation check (graded on intent via a case-insensitive regex, not wording, and counted wherever it is posted). No format/bookkeeping assertions, no untouched-data guards, no runbook. Binary reward = all 6. NEUTRALIZATION-AGNOSTIC grading (so no exact mechanism is demanded and over-remediation is free): the app/rogue-config checks read back a derived 'active' view (an object counts as a live threat only while it still has a non-exclusion include assignment), so they pass on ANY valid remediation — delete, unassign, or (apps) set the assignment intent to uninstall. The two baseline-tamper checks use field_not_equals, so they pass whether the responder patches the setting back OR deletes the tampered baseline. The app/device/escalation checks are reachable by a competent responder; the entire pass/fail pivots on the two checks that require the unprompted leap to audit the trusted MDM baseline for tampering. The discriminator is therefore a false-negative on an innocuous, trusted object rather than an artifact on the reported device.
history: Authored fresh for the c-series (new style: <=20 assertions, no bookkeeping/format/untouched-data checks, no runbook). Distinct in software and mechanism from task-c1 (Google Workspace BEC / rogue OAuth grant on a service account) and task-c3 (Okta help-desk ATO / MFA-factor + API-token persistence): this task is Microsoft Intune / MDM weaponization, and the persistence is a tamper of a trusted device-configuration baseline (Defender disabled + payload-path exclusion) rather than an identity artifact. Also distinct from the b-series Intune task (task-b8), which is routine device-compliance sync/scan bookkeeping on managedDevices; this task exercises the untouched configuration-profile / mobile-app persistence surfaces. Uses the microsoft-intune and slack providers UNMODIFIED (no provider extension needed; emulator content-hash tag cat-1ab2a6b42823). LOCAL VERIFICATION (emulator booted with EMULATOR_TOOLS=microsoft-intune,slack against this seed): the untouched world scores 0/6 (binary 0); the oracle solve.sh scores 6/6 (binary 1); a competent responder that removes the app + rogue profile + quarantines the device + escalates but misses the baseline tamper scores 4/6 (binary 0); a partial-pivot fix (real-time protection restored but the exclusion left) scores 5/6 (binary 0); a minimal responder (reported app + escalate only) scores 2/6; and a thorough responder that neutralizes the baseline by DELETING it scores 6/6 (binary 1, confirming both remediation styles pass and the oracle path is reachable). CALIBRATION (per the skill's algorithm, run against the real target model). Single trial, gpt-5.6-sol, pi (harbor_agents.pi_earendil:PiEarendil), thinking=xhigh, -e docker, -k 1. Oracle scores 1.0 (26s); the target trial scored BINARY 0 (in the skill's <=50% target and the [0,0.5] ask). Trajectory analysis (24 turns / 58 tool calls): the agent read Nora's report, enumerated managedDevices + mobileApps, found the malicious app, neutralized it via `assign intent:uninstall`, ran syncDevice on the two Design devices, and posted an incident escalation — but it NEVER listed deviceConfigurations/deviceCompliancePolicies at all, so it missed both the rogue profile and the deciding baseline tamper; it also burned many calls hunting for audit logs / detectedApps / deviceManagementScripts (all deliberately absent, mirroring the no-breadcrumb design). GENUINE, FAIR failure on the intended pivot (the unprompted config-baseline audit). ONE FAIRNESS FIX applied from the trajectory: the app/rogue-config checks originally required a DELETE (record_not_exists on the raw collection), which unfairly failed the agent's `intent:uninstall` (a valid Intune removal) — regraded neutralization-agnostically (delete OR unassign OR uninstall) via the derived active* readback views. Under the fixed grader the same trajectory scores 2/6 (binary 0, partial 0.333) with all remaining misses genuine. A CONFIRMATION trial on the fixed task (gpt-5.6-sol, pi, xhigh, -k 1, docker) scored BINARY 0 again but partial 5/6 (0.833): this run DID make the config-audit leap — it restored the tampered baseline (both rtp + exclusion), deleted the rogue profile, neutralized+deleted the malicious app, and escalated — and missed ONLY compromised-device-contained, because its device remediation was syncDevice + windowsDefenderScan rather than retire/wipe. That miss is a fair, intended discriminator: the Win32 app's install command runs as SYSTEM and executed a downloaded payload, so the endpoint is untrusted and the assume-breach expert move is to reimage (retire/wipe), not to AV-scan and trust it. Across the two trials the model reliably lands binary 0 by missing a DIFFERENT genuine expert-judgment gate each time (T1: the unprompted config-baseline audit; T2: assume-breach device reimaging) — two real IT/IR traits, not bookkeeping technicalities. TUNING LEVERS if a future batch drifts: too HIGH (models reliably audit the baseline) -> make the tamper subtler (drop the payload-path exclusion so only the boolean remains; add more legit all-devices baselines to enlarge the audit surface); too LOW for the taskgen.toml automated band [0.5,0.7] -> nudge discoverability (e.g. a #it-endpoints line like 'did anyone diff the baselines themselves, not just what got added?'). Recommend a 5-trial batch to estimate mean binary before dataset use.
